What To Do After Launching Your Website: The 10-Step Growth Order

By Noveliotech Team · Jun 8, 2026 · 9 min read · Business Growth

Growth Checklist Google Business Profile Lead Capture Follow-Up System

A website creates presence. But growth comes when the business has a complete system: traffic → lead capture → follow-up → conversion → review → repeat sales. Here is the exact order to build that system after your website goes live.

PriorityNext StepPurpose
1Google Business ProfileLocal visibility
2SEO basicsSearch visibility
3Lead captureConvert visitors
4CRM sheetTrack every lead
5Follow-up processIncrease sales
6Reviews / testimonialsBuild trust
7ContentLong-term growth
8AdsFaster lead generation
9Sales scriptBetter conversion
10DashboardControl growth

1. Google Business Profile

For most SMBs this is the first priority after the website. It drives local visibility, Google Maps ranking, calls and direction requests, reviews, trust, and direct local inquiries. If someone searches “CA near me” or “restaurant near me,” your profile can bring inquiries on its own.

2. Basic SEO Setup

Without SEO basics, the website may look good but remain invisible: page titles, meta descriptions, service and location keywords, image alt text, internal links, fast loading, mobile-friendly pages, Google Search Console setup, and sitemap submission.

3. Lead Capture System

Every visitor should have a clear action: WhatsApp button, call button, contact form, book-meeting link, quote request form, brochure download, and a thank-you page. The goal is simple: do not let visitors leave without a way to contact you.

4. CRM or Lead Tracking Sheet

This is where many SMBs fail — they get leads but do not track them. Track: name, mobile/email, lead source, requirement, budget, follow-up date, status, next action, and closing reason. A Google Sheet CRM is enough in the beginning.

5. Follow-Up Process

Most sales do not happen in the first call. A simple system: Day 0 first call/message · Day 1 reminder · Day 3 value message · Day 5 objection handling · Day 7 final offer/check-in · then weekly nurture. Bad follow-up kills good leads.

6. Review and Testimonial System

Trust converts faster than design. Collect Google reviews, video and written testimonials, before/after results, feedback screenshots, and case studies. This directly improves both website conversion and Google profile trust.

7. Content System

Blogs, FAQs, LinkedIn posts, short videos, case studies, industry tips, and problem-solution posts bring people into the funnel before they are ready to buy.

8. Paid Ads

Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, and retargeting — but only after the website, tracking, and lead capture are ready. Running ads before fixing the website and follow-up system is usually a waste of money.

9. Sales Script and Offer Clarity

Leads do not convert because of a website alone. You need a clear offer, pricing logic, sales pitch, objection answers, proposal format, closing script, and follow-up script. This turns inquiries into revenue.

10. Dashboard and Review System

Track weekly: website visitors, leads received, calls, lead sources, conversion rate, follow-ups pending, sales closed, revenue, cost per lead, and cost per sale. What is not measured does not improve.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the first priority after launching a website?

For most SMBs, the Google Business Profile: it drives local visibility, Maps ranking, calls, direction requests, reviews, and local lead generation.

When should a small business start running paid ads?

Only after the website, tracking, lead capture, and follow-up systems are ready. Ads amplify a working system — they cannot fix a broken one.

Do I need an expensive CRM to track leads?

No. A Google Sheet tracking name, contact, source, requirement, budget, follow-up date, status, and next action is enough in the beginning.
